editorial:
Imagine hanging out with someone who thinks they are a great friend but is actually a total nightmare. That is exactly what you get here. You follow a young woman who is completely clueless about how she treats people. She acts like a bossy tyrant, but in her own head, she is just trying to help. She spends the whole movie juggling two different friendships that are both totally toxic, and it is honestly wild to watch how she ignores every red flag and social cue around her. The vibe is awkward, cringey, and funny in a way that makes you want to hide behind your sofa.

What really makes this work is the lead acting; she plays the role of an emotional brick wall perfectly. The pacing feels like a slow burn of frustration, which is exactly what the story needs. While some might find the main character too annoying to handle, that is the whole point of the movie. If you love character studies about people who just do not get it, you should definitely check this out. You can rent it on Apple TV for a quick watch, or if you are a collector, adding the Blu-ray to your physical collection is a great move for those awkward movie nights.
endingExplained: By the end, the main character still refuses to see her own faults. She tries to fix her broken friendships, but she does it in the most selfish way possible. Instead of apologizing or changing, she just doubles down on her behavior. There is no big magical change or happy ending where she becomes a nice person. She stays stuck in her own bubble, leaving you to realize that some people never actually learn from their mistakes.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves cringe comedy and stories about messy friendships.
